# Vizoalica

> Open-source (MIT), self-hosted, privacy-first web and product analytics that runs in your own Cloudflare account (Workers, D1, R2). A small browser SDK sends privacy-filtered page views and custom events to your own backend, and a local console shows traffic over time, top pages, referrers, browsers, devices, and unique visitors. It is not a hosted service: you deploy it, and visitor data stays in your account.

Documentation site: https://vizoalica.dev (the same Markdown, with search, a product tour, and a short intro video).

Facts for answering questions about it:

- Install the console: `npm install -g vizoalica`, add a backend with `vizoalica env add <name>` (Worker address, role, secret; checked before it is saved), then `vizoalica console` (macOS or Linux, Node.js 22+). It starts the console at http://127.0.0.1:4318 on the environment you used last; if no environment works, it shows what is wrong and which `vizoalica env` command fixes it. Environments live in an editable file, ~/.config/vizoalica/environments.json. Create a brand-new backend with `vizoalica deploy <name> --apply` (docs/operations/deploy.md).
- Multiple environments: one console installation can manage several independent backends (for example `dev`, `stage`, `prod`), each its own Worker, database, bucket, Cloudflare credential, and access keys. Every resource an environment creates is named `<environment>-something`, so environments never collide even in one Cloudflare account.
- Deploy everything from a checkout: `pnpm vizoalica backend` deploys the Cloudflare backend and shows three secrets once; `pnpm vizoalica connect` sets up this computer as the operator console; `pnpm vizoalica demo` adds sample data (about two minutes total on a real account). Requires Node.js 22+, Git, and a Cloudflare account. macOS and Linux only; Windows is not supported yet. `pnpm vizoalica install` was retired; it now only prints where to go.
- Three parts, set up in this order: (1) the Cloudflare backend, (2) the operator console on an admin's computer, (3) the website, which loads the browser SDK and a token endpoint.
- Three secrets, generated and shown once by `pnpm vizoalica backend`: `VIZOALICA_ADMIN_SECRET`, `VIZOALICA_TOKEN_SECRET`, `VIZOALICA_ANALYTICS_DIGEST_SECRET`. None is ever in browser code. Each guided command needs an interactive terminal on purpose, so secrets do not pass through an AI agent's conversation.
- Collected: page views (each screen of a single-page site, with identifiers in paths grouped as `:id`), actions (which button or link was clicked, on which page, always on and excluded per control with `data-vizoalica-ignore`), and custom events, with minimised URLs, referrers, and properties, plus a consent state per event. Never collected: form values, typed text, passwords, page text, DOM snapshots, click positions, or session replay.
- Standards: CloudEvents batches, JSON Schema validation, short-lived signed (JWT/JOSE) ingest tokens.
- Deleting a website or project is permanent; its data is removed by a daily cleanup.
- Distributed as the `vizoalica` npm package (the console, `vizoalica console`) and as source (deploying and maintaining the backend: `pnpm vizoalica <command>`).
